subject: Follow-up: CarePath pricing scope & host comparison
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Mills <jared@carepath.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-15T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: CarePath pricing scope & host comparison

Jared — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

- Volume profile (what we heard): pilot ~1.5M tokens/month, production expected to scale to ~6–10M tokens/month within 9–12 months.
- Primary workloads: patient triage summaries (short prompts, many requests) + nightly batch processing for analytics (longer context).
- Primary constraint: procurement is targeting predictable unit economics; security/compliance (SOC2) is required.

Open asks for you so we can build a formal commercial:
1) Confirm the 1.5M pilot/week or month? (we logged month in notes)
2) Target budget range for $/1M tokens at pilot and at steady-state (band is fine)
3) Any hard limits on self-hosting or must be fully managed (private VPC)?

Attached are our quick discovery notes from the call for your review (carepath-ma-discovery-notes.pdf). If you can confirm items 1–3 today/tomorrow we’ll push a benchmarked price schedule showing: dedicated reserved pricing, burstable pricing, and comparable public-host pricing (OpenAI/Anthropic/selected open-hosts).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm the budget band + hosting preference
- We send a 1-page price/ops play (incl. comparative host rates)
- If it looks good, book a procurement-specific call to walk legal and SRE through details

Thanks — Alex

Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the recap and the notes. Small clarifications:

- Pilot is 1.5M tokens/month (not week).
- Target budget for pilot: roughly $800–$1,200 per 1M tokens. That’s what procurement is comfortable approving for a short pilot if we can demonstrate latency & cost controls.
- Steady-state (6–10M): procurement is looking for something in the $400–$700/1M range, contingent on commitments and SLAs.

We definitely need SOC2 evidence and a short note on data residency (we prefer US-only). Also: Jared here, copying procurement channel for any formal intake (procurement@carepath.com).

Open question: we asked the SRE lead if a private VPC is preferred — they said managed VPC is fine as long as keys remain customer-controlled.

Appreciate a benchmark vs OpenAI/Anthropic and any open-hosts you think are comparable. Jared

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Mills <jared@carepath.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-16T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: CarePath pricing scope & host comparison

Jared — great, thanks for confirming. See a short benchmark summary below (attached CSV has a simple per-1M breakdown tuned to typical prompt mixes):

Quick benchmark (per 1M tokens, approximate list rates / public host comparator):
- OpenAI (latest large-gen family, managed API): $1,200–$2,000 per 1M (varies by model and context length)
- Anthropic (Claude-family managed): $900–$1,500 per 1M
- Selected open-hosts (hosted open models / community hosts): $400–$1,000 per 1M depending on quantization and instance mix

What Redwood would propose for CarePath (draft, contingent on commitment + region & SLA):
- Pilot (1.5M/mo, no long-term commit): $900/1M with managed VPC and SOC2 evidence delivered; includes prefix cache optimizations to reduce tail spend.
- Committed reserved (12-month, 6M baseline commit): $650/1M with burst allowance and prioritized capacity; includes dedicated pool and customer-managed KMS for keys.
- Steady-state target band (6–10M, with escalation discounts at 10M+): $450–$650/1M depending on commit/throughput profile and batching/caching settings.

Notes on comparators: open-hosts can be cheaper but often lack guaranteed capacity and have higher variance in latency. Managed public-hosts (OpenAI/Anthropic) are typically higher list price but include the convenience of single-API access and broad model choice. Our Delta to open-hosts is justified by reliability guarantees, SLA-backed latency targets, and tooling for controlling per-token cost (auto-batching, KV cache).

Attached: 1M-token-benchmark-table.csv (shows modeled spend across 3 prompt mixes and different commit levels). I can convert this into a 1-pager price play for procurement if you’d like.

If these ranges look plausible, next steps we recommend:
1) Jared/procurement to confirm pilot OK at $900/1M (or counter)
2) If pilot approved, we draft a short commercial term sheet + SOC2 evidence packet and schedule procurement call
3) Ben/Laura will help fast-track any discounts or reserved-commit packaging once procurement confirms numbers

Best — Alex

Alex Martinez

- Approve SOC2 packet to be attached to the commercial email to CarePath.

Alex — please prepare the 1-page commercial with the anchor $900 pilot and an optional reserved path at $650 w/ 12mo commit. Also include a short bullet on expected unit economics improvement via KV caching (we should quantify expected 15–25% token saving for triage flows if possible).

Ben Carter
